title: Desk Guide — RideLink Lodging and Meals on a Long-Distance Stay
content:
Non-Emergency Medical Transportation reimburses lodging and meals when a member's long-distance trip includes an overnight stay. The desk books this reimbursement as an approved lodging and meals entry on the member's reimbursement ledger.

## When the entry is booked

A lodging and meals entry is booked for a registered long-distance trip whose one-way miles are at least the level's lodging threshold and whose stay includes at least one lodging night, and it is worked out from that trip's registered outbound and return legs, which are the member's latest registered legs of each kind. Lodging and meals on such a stay are paid as allowances, whatever the receipts show.

The entry records the trip's reservation number, the round trip as its leg, the outbound leg's appointment date as its trip date, the lodging nights and the travel days.

**Effect.** The approved lodging and meals entry stands on the reimbursement ledger with a new member reimbursement claim number and is owed to the member until it is paid. The member sees the approved claim, its number and amount in their reimbursement history.

## The booking tool

The entry is booked with `approve_stay_lodging_meals_3bb3a021`, an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`. One call books one approved lodging and meals claim, dated today; nothing else on the benefit changes.

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `ride_benefit_id` | Reference number of the member's transportation benefit, as the transportation benefit lookup returns it for the verified member | Identifier |
| `trip_number` | The trip's reservation number, as on the trip's registered legs or the member's confirmation | Verbatim, character for character (for example RL-5580213) |
| `leg` | Which part of the trip the claim covers | One of `outbound` (home to the appointment only), `return` (back home only), `round_trip` (the whole trip out and back, as a lodging and meals claim for a stay does), `not_applicable` (no trip leg) |
| `reimbursement_type` | The kind of reimbursement | One of `lodging_meals` (the kind this booking records), `mileage`, `late_pickup_alternative`, `not_applicable` (kinds this booking never records) |
| `claim_trip_date` | The trip date the claim is for | YYYY-MM-DD, a calendar date with no time or time zone |
| `lodging_nights` | The lodging nights approved | Whole number, zero or more |
| `meal_days` | The travel days approved for meals | Whole number, zero or more |
| `amount` | The approved reimbursement amount | USD, 2 decimal places, positive; stored rounded to 2 decimals exactly as passed |

**Return.** A text dictionary: `status` is the literal "approved" when the claim was booked, which is the success receipt; `reimbursement_claim_number` is the new claim number in the form MR-YYMMDD-NNNN; `ledger_entry` is the reference of the new ledger entry; `trip_number`, `leg`, `reimbursement_type` and `claim_trip_date` echo what was booked; `lodging_nights` and `meal_days` are the integers booked; `amount` is the approved USD amount with 2 decimals; `posted_date` is today's date as YYYY-MM-DD.

*Illustrative call shape (hypothetical values):* benefit reference as looked up, `trip_number` RL-5580213, `leg` `round_trip`, `reimbursement_type` `lodging_meals`, `claim_trip_date` 2026-03-10, `lodging_nights` 3, `meal_days` 4, and the approved amount.
